title: Best Climate Crisis Project
description: During the last century, the accelerated rising of Earth's average air temperature due to the combustion of fossil fuels has had disastrous effects on the global climate. Can synthetic biology be applied to develop carbon fixation technologies which remove greenhouse gasses like CO₂ and CFCs from the atmosphere? Can we improve the existing energy sources, or industrial and agricultural processes to reduce the emission of pollutants like methane or nitrous oxide in the first place? What other approaches to addressing the climate crisis are possible with synthetic biology?

title: Best Environment Project
description: The quality of land, water, and air limits the happiness of Earth's inhabitants. Can biotechnology be used to help clean the air, provide fresh drinking water, or prevent the accumulation of antibiotics and antibiotic resistant microorganisms in the environment?

title: Best Bioremediation Project
description: Human dependence on petroleum products, unsafe agricultural practices, and rapid industrialization have led to the accumulation of toxic pollutants that harm the environment and threaten public health. Can your team use synthetic biology to harness the power of microorganisms or plants to detoxify contaminants in the air, water, soil, flue gasses, and industrial effluents?

title: Best Conservation Project
description: Environmental destruction, monocultures in agriculture, disease, and other human activities have affected the health of plants, animals, and their ecosystems for a long time. How can synthetic biology be applied to the protection of endangered species, or the reversal of anthropogenic extinctions?

title: Best Agriculture Project
description: In the coming decades, agriculture must both feed the growing global population and implement sustainable practices to ensure a healthy environment. This challenge has become more difficult as the increased frequency and intensity of extreme weather events has led to lower crop yields, reduced soil fertility, and more pests and diseases. How will your team apply synthetic biology to revolutionize agriculture and improve the quality and quantity of food?

title: Best Food & Nutrition Project
description: Everybody needs to eat. But with over 7 billion people on the planet, the problem of producing enough food is complex and multi-faceted. Can biotechnology be responsibly used to reduce food waste, or produce food or nutritional molecules without causing widespread shortages of either, and without harming the environment that future generations will inherit?

title: Best Diagnostics Project
description: Many medical conditions can be successfully treated if only they are diagnosed at an early enough stage. Diagnostic technologies also play a key role in preventive healthcare, public health, and epidemiology. Can your team come up with faster, cheaper and better diagnostics techniques to improve access to medical treatment worldwide?

title: Best Therapeutics Project
description: Many health and medical problems can best be addressed with new and novel therapies. What can synthetic biology do to improve techniques, technology and access to novel therapies?

title: Best Foundational Advance Project
description: iGEM relies on a number of foundational technologies to function. We use BioBricks, standardization (RFCs), high-throughput quality control and many other processes to run the competition. The Foundational Advance track allows teams to come up with novel solutions to technical problems surrounding core synbio technologies. For example, the discovery and application of DNA recombination allowed us to assemble new genes. What are other types of basic tricks does nature use? Have you discovered and applied one that could revolutionize synthetic biology?

title: Best Biomanufacturing Project
description: What can biology be programmed to manufacture? Biological systems can be used to make products under conditions that were previously impossible. Many enzymes can achieve reaction conditions in a tube that would otherwise require high temperatures, pressures or expensive substrates to reproduce using chemical engineering methods. Could we use synthetic biology to manufacture useful products, perform micro-scale production of high-value molecules like therapeutics, or produce engineered tissues such as new skin or organs?

title: Best Software & AI Project
description: If you are going to design a new life form, chances are you'll need a computer to design the smallest genetic circuits and deal with genome-scale complexity. Artificial intelligence and machine learning promise to bring a new level of computational power to synthetic biology. The software track is for computer scientists and developers to nurture their knowledge of biology, and for computational biologists, bioinformaticians and biologists to enhance their aptitude for building software. What will you build?

title: Best New Basic Part
description: Most genetically-encoded functions have not yet been converted to BioBrick parts. Thus, there are many opportunities to find new, cool, and important genetically encoded functions, and refine and convert the DNA encoding these functions into BioBrick standard biological parts. To be eligible for this award, this part will consist of a single genetic component and be supported by documentation on the Main Page on the Part's Page on the Registry. Winning parts are highly documented with experimental details and data showing the part working. See parts BBa_K863006 and BBa_K863001 as examples.

title: Best New Composite Part
description: New BioBrick devices can be made by combining existing BioBrick Parts. For example, Inverters, Amplifiers, Smell Generators, Protein Balloon Generators, Senders, Receivers, Actuators, and so on. To be eligible for this award, this part will consist of a combination of genetic components and be supported by documentation on the Main Page on the Part's Page on the Registry. Winning parts are highly documented with experimental details and data showing the part working. See parts BBa_K404122 and BBa_K863005 as examples.

title: Best New Improved Part
description: The Registry is rich with engineering opportunities. Can you redesign an existing part to create a new part with improved function? Can you show the improvement in an experiment by using the original part as a control? To be eligible for this award, this part must be well-documented on the Main Page on the Part's Page on the Registry. Winning parts are highly documented with experimental details and data showing the new part works better than the old part when measured in the same experiment. See this pair of parts as an example: existing part from 2016 (BBa_K2116002) and improved part from 2022 (BBa_K4387000).

title: Best Part Collection
description: The Registry is rich with engineering opportunities. Can you redesign an existing part to create a new part with improved function? Can you show the improvement in an experiment by using the original part as a control? To be eligible for this award, this part must be well-documented on the Main Page on the Part's Page on the Registry. Winning parts are highly documented with experimental details and data showing the new part works better than the old part when measured in the same experiment. See this pair of parts as an example: existing part from 2016 (BBa_K2116002) and improved part from 2022 (BBa_K4387000).

title: Best Measurement
description: Measurements are critical to scientific communication and advancement. Well-reported measurements are the only way to show whether hardware is functioning correctly, whether data are reliable, and whether a result is actually important. There is a high value in identifying appropriate targets for measurement, collecting precise measurements, and reporting results clearly and with appropriate units. Document your careful measurement efforts and you could win this award!

title: Best Model
description: Models and computer simulations can help us understand the function and operation of BioBrick Parts and Devices. Simulation and modeling are critical engineering skills that can contribute to project design or provide a better understanding of the modeled process. These processes are even more useful and/or informative when real world data are included in the model. This award is for teams who build a model of their system and use it to inform system design or simulate expected behavior before, or in conjunction with, experiments in the wetlab.

title: Best Hardware
description: This is a prize for the team that has developed a piece of hardware for synthetic biology. Hardware in iGEM should make synthetic biology based on standard parts easier, faster, better or more accessible to our community. Did your team make a sensor to help teams characterize parts? Did you make a robot that can help teams perform experiments or do cloning more easily? Tell us what your team did for this award!

title: Best Software Tool
description: Regardless of what's the topic, iGEM projects often create or adapt computational tools to move the bigger project forward. Because they are born out of a direct practical need, these software tools (or new computational methods) can even prove surprisingly useful for others. Without necessarily being big or complex, they can make the crucial difference to a project's success. This award tries to find and honor such "nuggets" of computational work. To be eligible, your software has to be documented and made available under an OSI-approved open source license.

title: Best Plant Synthetic Biology
description: This award is designed to celebrate exemplary work done in plant synthetic biology. Did you build a project in a plant chassis? Did you submit plant parts to the Registry? This award could also be given to a team working with algae or another eukaryotic photosynthetic chassis. Show us what you made and remember to adhere to iGEM safety guidelines!

title: Safety and Security Award
description: Synthetic biology will need to be used safely and securely if local people are to solve local problems all around the world. The Safety and Security Committee is challenging teams to apply biological engineering approaches to manage risks associated with synthetic biology. Can you take the next step in incremental progress towards knowledge, understanding, and tools that will make the use of synthetic biology safer and more secure?

title: Best Integrated Human Practices
description: How does your project affect society and how does society influence the direction of your project? How might ethical considerations and stakeholder input guide your project purpose, design, and experiments you conduct in the lab? How does this feedback enter into the process of your work all through the iGEM competition? Document a thoughtful and creative approach to exploring these questions and how your project evolved in the process to compete for this award.

title: Best Entrepreneurship
description: The entrepreneurship prize recognizes exceptional effort to build a business case and commercialize an iGEM project. This award can go to a new project or to a previous project that a team aimed to commercialize. Have you filed a provisional patent on your project/device/process? Have you raised money to build and ship products? Have you pitched your idea to investors and received money? Complete the entrepreneurship section on the Judging form and impress the judges with what you did!

title: Best Sustainable Development Impact
description: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a call to action to integrally address global environmental, social, and economic challenges. iGEM teams can answer this call with this prize. Demonstrate how you have evaluated your project ideas against one or more of the SDGs, how you've consulted with SDG stakeholders, and how you've begun to form collaborations with other iGEM teams around the SDGs. You're encouraged to look back at previous iGEM projects to evaluate them against the SDGs and build upon them.

title: Inclusivity Award
description: The Inclusivity Award recognizes exceptional efforts to include people with diverse identities in scientific research. Who is allowed to have a voice in iGEM, synthetic biology, and science more broadly? How have you developed new opportunities to eliminate barriers and allow more people to contribute to, participate in, and/or be represented by these communities? To compete for this prize, activities do not have to be directly related to your team's project. Document your approach, how you improved inclusivity, and what was learned.

title: Best Presentation
description: Presentations should be clear, engaging, and communicate your project to a scientific/engineering community. Can your team tell your story and present your data in a concise and visually appealing way?

title: Best Wiki
description: The team Wiki is the “face” of your iGEM project. The team Wikis serve as the main project information resource for future iGEM students and teams, as well as the rest of the world. This award honors the team Wiki that exemplifies what the following year's Wikis should strive for.

title: Best Education
description: How have you developed new opportunities to include more people in shaping synthetic biology? Innovative educational tools and outreach activities have the ability to establish a two-way dialogue with new communities by discussing public values and the science behind synthetic biology. Document your approach and what was learned by everyone involved to compete for this award.

title: iGEMers Prize
description: The iGEMers' prize is voted on by this year's iGEM teams to celebrate their favorite teams. Each iGEM team receives a voting ballot to select a team (other than their own!) that they believe best represents the iGEM values. The choice is yours!

title: Best Project Promotion Video
description: The Project Promotion Video summarizes a team’s project, introducing the problem the team is addressing, their solution, and its impact. The best project promotion prize rewards creative use of video, quality production, and clear communication of the team’s project. You are welcome to put on your thinking caps and share your journey with unbounded creativity to a broad audience!
